units.title: gilliver chippy fog hours
units.author: gilliver_teen
units.text: official chippy announcement since im the only one who posts them. closing at 9 tonight not 10 because the boss says nobody walks down harbour road in fog and he's not frying for ghosts. last orders 8:45. the curry sauce is the good batch. you're welcome gilliver

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Aye, I was in at half seven. Haddock was right. Tell your boss the street lights by the slip are flickering again, so it's darker than usual down that end. Folk'll not come down for chips if they can't see the step.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: Thank you, young man, for the hours. Would you please tell your employer that the woman with the walking stick who comes in on Wednesdays would be very grateful if he kept a small portion of fish back for her at a quarter to nine. She will not be walking down in the fog any later than that. She will tip.

units.title: Mill Lane power off this morning (planned).
units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Planned cut on Mill Lane and the east of the market square, nine to one. Questions: 1. Did it come back on time? (I'm at work.) 2. My freezer: is four hours all right if nobody opens it? 3. Has anyone else's doorbell started playing a tune by itself since? Ours played the first bar of something at 13:05 and stopped.

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: I'm on Kiln Row, two doors from the square. Finding 1: power returned at 12:51, nine minutes early. Finding 2: a full freezer keeps safe for around a day if the door stays shut; four hours is nothing. Finding 3: your doorbell is the kind with a battery backup that plays its stored tune when power returns. Ours does it too. I apologise for the format, it's a habit.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: That's the most useful post anyone has ever written to me, thank you, findings and all. Freezer fine, peas fine, doorbell explained. The children are disappointed; they had decided the house was saying hello. I've told them it was saying 'the power's back', which is a kind of hello.

units.title: Visitor bays again
units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: For the record, as nobody else will keep one. A white van has been parked across the two visitor bays since yesterday evening. There is no visitor. I have left a note under the wiper. The note is still there. Meanwhile my daughter, who is a visitor, had to park on Canal Street, where she got a ticket. I will be raising this at any meeting that has chairs.

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Thanks, Mr Pryce, noted for the meeting along with the stairwell and the lift, I promise the bays won't be forgotten. Please don't put any more notes on the van; if it's still there tomorrow I'll ring Kerrow Estates, as the bays are theirs to enforce. Bev, DCRA

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Second day. Note still under the wiper, now damp. The engine was running at seven this morning with nobody in the front. Either the driver is asleep in the back or he is a very considerate thief. I have not put another note on. I have put a cup of tea on the bonnet, which is a different thing entirely.

units.title: Fur windshields in fog: they get soaked. Ideas?
units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so practical question. my fluffy windshield is a sponge in this fog, after an hour it's heavy and the mic sounds like it's under a duvet. do people just accept it or is there a trick? I'm going out most nights this week so I need something that doesn't cost a month's wages, I work at a school

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: In still fog you don't need the fur. There's no wind. Use the foam, keep a dry one in a sandwich bag and swap it at midnight. Fur's for wind. Fog's just wet. Also tape a bit of plastic over the top of the stand like a little roof. Looks daft. Works.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Seconding the roof. I made one out of a takeaway lid for my binaural head and now it looks like it's wearing a little hat, which delights children on the towpath. Also pop a sachet of silica gel in the recorder pouch, it stops the buttons going sticky.

units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: In 1974 we wrapped the microphone in a lady's stocking, which the lady was not consulted about. It worked very well in damp weather and was not much worse in the wind. I do not recommend the method as a whole, but I recommend the stocking. Regards, Ned

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so I now have: a foam in a sandwich bag, a takeaway-lid roof, two silica sachets, and a story from Ned I will never forget. thank you all. tested in the garden tonight, it works. the mic now looks like a tiny chef

units.title: Driving in fog: rules from the road
units.author: lh_trucker_orrin
units.text: Saw some of you up north have fog all week. Rules from forty years on the road: 1. Dipped lights, not full, full just lights the fog. 2. Follow the edge line, not the tail lights in front, they'll take you into a ditch with them. 3. Window down an inch so you can hear. 4. If you see something at the edge of your lights, it's a post. It's always a post. Slow down anyway.

units.author: lh_taxi_halvard
units.text: number 4 is the truest thing on the forum Merle, I've braked for a lot of posts. one night by the river I braked for a man in a grey coat and it turned out to be a man in a grey coat, very surprised, waiting for a bus that wasn't coming. gave him a lift. anyway

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: the night buses at the depot have got a rule that if a driver sees something in the road they stop and the cleaners go out and look, so I've been out in the fog with a torch to look at a bin bag, a fox, and once a whole sofa, love, a sofa, on the ring road at four in the morning, I still think about who put it there

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Adding rule 5 for my drive home past the Brackwater junction: when the temporary lights are red in fog, you can't see them until you're on top of them, so assume red. They're always red. I've timed it at four minutes. I sit there and count the cones. Fog makes the cones look like little people, which doesn't help at 05:10.

units.title: A clear night on the gallery
units.author: lh_lighttender_tamsin
units.text: A clear, still night on our coast, the opposite of what I read you have up north. The beam goes out a long way tonight and lays a pale road across the water, and on nights like this I can see the line of the shore three miles off, the rocks and the white of the surf. It is very beautiful and very quiet. The kettle in the service room is the only other thing awake.

units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: same coast! I can't see your light from the call centre, it's an industrial estate with no windows, but I can picture it now. between calls I'm going to imagine the pale road. it's better than the hold music, which tonight is a pan pipe version of a song about a lighthouse, I'm not joking

units.title: fog rota, night boat
units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Fog rota for the night boat, as agreed with the skipper. Forward lookout: me on the Gilliver legs, Finn on the Lisle legs, swap at midnight. Loud-hailer stays at the wheelhouse door. Good torch charged and in the locker, not in someone's pocket. Hot drinks every hour for whoever's forward. If you're cold, say so; a frozen lookout is no lookout.

units.author: deckhand_finn
units.text: agreed except the bit about saying if you're cold because I'll be saying it constantly and you'll stop listening. torch is in the locker, I checked, it was in my pocket. sorry. hot drinks every hour is the best rule we've ever had

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: spare thermos at the chandlery for the night boat if anyone wants to pick it up, on the house this once. bring it back. last one went to lisle and came back with soup in it, which was nice, but still

units.title: Vending machine report: fog edition
units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: B corridor machine has eaten three of my coins tonight and given me a hot chocolate that tastes of soup. The A&E machine is out of everything except mints. The one by the mortuary lift works perfectly and always has, which none of us will discuss. Fog outside's like porridge. Quiet in A&E so far, touch wood. Tea's the only thing that works on this site.

units.author: lh_picker_weyhaven
units.text: our machine at the depot takes the card, thinks about it, says 'transaction declined', then gives you the crisps anyway. we've reported it. we are lying. nobody has reported it. it is the only perk of this job and we will protect it with our lives

units.title: Found: house key on a red ribbon, Harbour Parade.
units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: While putting up Pebble posters on Harbour Parade this morning I found a single brass house key on a red ribbon, lying by the bench opposite the ferry terminal. It's in an envelope behind the counter at the florist's on Market Street. If it's yours, come and describe the ribbon. I'll keep it safe.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Moved to Lost & Found. Thank you for doing it the right way: not posting a photo of a key that could open someone's house. Anyone claiming it should describe the ribbon and the key, please. Pell.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: That's mine. Red ribbon, a knot tied in it twice because I kept losing it, and the key has a little nick near the top where I used it to open a tin of paint. I dropped it running for the 17:45 on day four. I'll come by the florist's tomorrow lunchtime. Thank you, and good luck with Pebble.

units.title: Tuesday night check-in: where are you and what's the weather?
units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Mid-week check-in, everyone. Where are you, what are you drinking, and what's outside the window? I'm at the pharmacy counter, Coriveth, mint tea, harbour wind and a delivery boy asleep on the bench outside, which I'm told is normal. Housekeeping as always: be kind, drink water, stories are fine, prophecy isn't.

units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: Port Ammet General, builders' tea, fog so thick on the hospital roof I couldn't see the car park from the stairwell window. The Carrow foghorn is going every thirty seconds and one of the night sisters has started humming along. Busy-ish. Back to the run.

units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: Coriveth harbour bakery, strong black coffee, and outside is the same harbour wind Ines has, carrying flour off our step. Rye loaves in, sourdough shaped and resting like sleeping cats. The delivery boy on her bench is ours, by the way. We'll wake him at four with a roll. He's earned it.

units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: Vellmark, 400 metres down, flask of something that used to be coffee. No window. Weather is rock. Will report the sky at six.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Got a full tank first thing, before Dacre's boat. Treloar was there too and we shared the flask. Price held at yesterday's. Dacre's lad says the island crew asked for a crate of tea on the last boat, more than they asked for chains. Sensible people.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Tea before chains is the correct order of operations on any job, ask any engine room. Our office has been on at me about fuel use in fog. Slow ahead burns less per hour, yes, but the crossing takes nearly twice as long and the gensets, heating and floods run the whole time, so the day's total goes up. They've asked me to explain it again in writing. Pray for me.

units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: Sky report, as promised, from the bus: black, clear, stars like spilled salt, minus four. The pump on level 4 behaved itself. Liv's on the next bus. The bus driver said 'morning', out loud, a new development. I said it back. We may be friends.

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Fair enough Bram, cheers for the honest answer. Not put off though, the rate's the rate and I've done a winter on the Brackwater forestry before. If anyone hears Grieve are short of hands, I'm about. Otherwise hedges in Tollinby as usual, no job too small, reasonable rates, own kit.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Brackwater's got a road and a pub, Davey. The Holm's got a beach that dries for two hundred yards and the dark. It's not the same winter. But you'll do as you like. Couldn't hear the saws today at all, the fog's too thick, it just swallowed them.

units.author: lh_lighttender_tamsin
units.text: Hana, a pan-pipe song about a lighthouse is a cruelty, and I'm sorry. Another clear night here. Just after two a walker came along the cliff path, the way they sometimes do, and stood for a while where the beam passes over, then went on. I always wave. I don't think they ever see it. The kettle has boiled twice.

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: The van has gone. So has the cup. The cup has been returned, washed, to my doormat with a note that says 'thanks mate, sorry about the bays'. I don't know what to do with this information. My daughter's parking ticket remains unpaid as a matter of principle.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: Rota holding well three nights in. Lookouts have been sharp and nobody's frozen. Thank you to the chandlery for the thermos and to the Lisle pier for the kettle. Two changes from tonight: lookout swap at 23:00 instead of midnight, and the forward flood goes on the slip from further out at Gilliver. Logged, carried on.

units.author: lh_trucker_orrin
units.text: Lorna, a sofa on the ring road at four in the morning is the best thing I've read on here. I once found a whole wedding cake on the shoulder outside a truck stop, three tiers, untouched, little figures on top. Nobody ever claimed it. I didn't eat it. I thought about it for two hundred miles.

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: if it helps the rota... I'll have the kettle on at the Lisle pier hut from ten every night this week, so whoever's forward on the Lisle leg can nip in for two minutes while you're tied up. ha, anyway, it's a big kettle, there's enough for the skipper too

units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear Ivy, my neighbour printed your drawing for me, as I do not see well on the small screen. You have the green button exactly. My husband used to call it the night-light for giants. I would like to buy the drawing, if you would sell it, and I would hang it by my door. Irena, 7C

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: I was on the Mill Lane job, so a late confirmation: we were done at 12:45 and switched back at 12:51, all good. Ledger's right about the doorbells; a lot of the wireless ones replay their chime on reboot. We had three people come out of their houses to tell us their doorbell had 'said hello'. That's the nicest feedback we've had in weeks.
